record.exact_statement: Let C* be the best FEI constant (possibly infinite), K* = sup over nonconstant g of min_{i: d_i>0} D_i/d_i, and K*_lambda the same with lambda_i. Then C* <= K* <= C* + min(2/ln 2, C*) and C* - 3/ln 2 <= K*_lambda <= C*. Pointwise for nonconstant g: min_i D_i/d_i <= H/I + min(2/ln 2, H/I) and min_i lambda_i/d_i <= (sum_i B_i)/I <= H/I. Equivalently, FEI holds iff there is an absolute K such that every f has a coordinate i with KL(nu_i||q_i) >= log2(1/Inf_i(f)) - K.

record.exact_statement: For every complete tree and every coordinate rule, E sum_t (D_t - C d_t) = H(f) - C I(f); for a stopping tree it equals (H(f)-C I(f)) - E[H(g_tau) - C I(g_tau)]. The minimal nonnegative potential Q*_v = max(0, D_v - C d_v + avg Q*_children) (Q*=0 at leaves) satisfies D_t <= C d_t + Q_t - E[Q_{t+1}|F_t], is dominated by every nonnegative potential with that property, and gives H(f) <= C I(f) + Q*_root; Q*_root = 0 under the greedy D/d rule whenever C >= K*. Hence positive expected whole-path debt on a complete tree is exactly a counterexample to H <= C I, independent of the rule, and stopping-rule falsifiers can only target Q*.

record.exact_statement: Let f be a Boolean function on n bits, N > n, x0 in {-1,1}^N, p = 2^(-N), and g_N(x) = f(x_1..x_n)(1 - 2*1{x = x0}). (a) ghat_N(S) = fhat(S)*1{S subset [n]} - 2p f(x0) chi_S(x0) for every S subset [N]; for every A subset [N] the coefficient of g_N*chi_A at [N] is nonzero, so d_{g_N chi_A}(S) = N for every S and every anchor A, and U(g_N) = N Var(g_N) - I(g_N). (b) |I_i(g_N) - I_i(f)| <= 2p for every i, so |I(g_N) - I(f)| <= 2Np. (c) the spectral laws satisfy ||p(g_N) - p(f)||_1 <= 4p(2^(n/2) + 1), and |H(g_N) - H(f)| <= eps N + h2(eps) with eps = 2p(2^(n/2) + 1). (d) for nonconstant f, H(g_N) -> H(f), I(g_N) -> I(f) and U(g_N)/I(g_N) -> infinity. (e) if psi(s,N) >= 0 with max_s psi(s,N) = o(2^N) and Psi(g) = sum over nonempty S with ghat(S) != 0 of ghat(S)^2 psi(|S|, d_g(S)), then Psi(g_N) - sum_{S nonempty} fhat(S)^2 psi(|S|, N) -> 0; hence an inequality H <= alpha I + beta Var + Psi valid for all Boolean functions implies H(f) <= alpha I(f) + beta Var(f) + liminf_N sum_{S nonempty} fhat(S)^2 psi(|S|, N) for all Boolean f. (f) FEI with constant C on the class {g_N} implies FEI with constant C for all Boolean functions.

Consequently for complete trees H(f)-(3/ln2)I(f) <= sum_v w_v Q_v <= H(f): the retained-KL tree target sum_v w_v M_v[log2(1/M_v)-D_2(nu_v||q_v)]=O(I) (ISOSPECTRAL (8.1)) holds for one complete tree iff it holds for every tree iff FEI holds, with constants shifted by at most 3/ln2.

record.proof_source: Per coordinate c at position p: ln(p/N_p) >= 0 with N_p = |S intersect pi^{-1}[1,p]|; Jensen gives E[1{c in S} ln(p/N_p)] >= P(c in S) max{0, ln p - ln E[N_p | c in S]}; P(c in S) = 2^(1-L); given c in S its block's other members are in S independently with prob 1/2 and other blocks are independent, so E[N_p | c in S] <= (L+1)/2 + (p-1) 2^(1-L). H(AND_L)/I(AND_L) <= 4 - [4 + 2(L-1)eps - 2(1-eps)/ln2]/L < 4 with eps = 2^(1-L). The liminf follows from the increasing integrand phi(t) = ln t - ln(c - q + q t).
